caption: The Components panel lists Salesforce's standard components first — but a custom one, built by a developer, drags onto the canvas exactly the same way.
‘Opportunity Alerts’ isn't a standard Salesforce feature — it's a Lightning web component, dragged onto this app's home page like any other.
The exact same custom component, now on the Salesforce mobile layout — the App Builder canvas previews both without any separate mobile build.

code:
Platform App Builder:
  drags components onto the canvas
  sets exposed properties (which list, which filter)
  decides WHERE a component goes

Developer:
  writes the Lightning web component itself
  decides WHAT the component can do

Neither role replaces the other.
caption: You don't need to write a component to use one — but you do need to know what “exposed property” means.
